content: 1. When co-administering cenobamate with CYP3A4 substrates, increase the dose of the substrate as needed and monitor the patient closely. 2. Ritonavir increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is serious, and alternative medications should be considered. 3. Ritonavir also increases ceritinib levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs in this case. 4. Ceritinib can increase ritonavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Ritonavir increases cetirizine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Ritonavir increases cevimeline levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 7. Chloramphenicol increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Ritonavir increases chlordiazepoxide levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider lowering benzodiazepine doses due to potential toxicity. 9. Ritonavir increases chlorpromazine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 10. Ritonavir increases cholic acid toxicity by reducing its elimination. Avoid using inhibitors of the bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) and monitor liver function tests if co-administration is necessary. 11. Ritonavir increases inhaled ciclesonide levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. 12. Ritonavir increases cilostazol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Cimetidine increases ritonavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Ritonavir increases cinacalcet levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Ritonavir increases citalopram levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of serotonin syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended, especially with QT-prolonging drugs. 16. Clarithromycin increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is serious, and alternative medications should be considered. 17. Ritonavir increases clomipramine levels by affecting both CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Ritonavir increases clonazepam levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider lowering benzodiazepine doses due to potential toxicity. 19. Ritonavir decreases clopidogrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4, reducing clopidogrel bioactivation. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Clotrimazole decreases ritonavir levels by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Ritonavir increases clozapine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Cobicistat increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 23. Ritonavir increases cobimetinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 24. Ritonavir increases topical cocaine levels by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Ritonavir decreases codeine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, preventing its conversion to morphine. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ritonavir increases colchicine levels by affecting both P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, especially in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 27. Ritonavir increases conivaptan levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 28. Ritonavir increases conjugated estrogens levels by affecting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Ritonavir increases copanlisib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 30. Ritonavir increases cortisone levels by affecting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Ritonavir increases crizotinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 32. Crofelemer increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 in the gut. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Ritonavir increases cyclophosphamide levels by affecting both CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Monitor closely. 34. Ritonavir increases cyclosporine levels by affecting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Ritonavir increases dabigatran levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration in patients with reduced renal function (CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment). 36. Ritonavir increases dabrafenib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Dacomitinib increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 38. Danazol increases ritonavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 39. Danicopan increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Ritonavir increases dapsone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 41. Ritonavir increases daridorexant levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 42. Darifenacin increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Ritonavir increases darolutamide levels by affecting both P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for adverse reactions and adjust darolutamide dosing as needed. 44. Darunavir increases ritonavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 45. Dasatinib increases ritonavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Adjust dasatinib dosing if co-administration is necessary. 46. Ritonavir increases daunorubicin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Ritonavir decreases deferasirox levels by inducing UGT enzymes. Avoid co-administration with potent UGT inducers. If necessary, increase the deferasirox dose and monitor ferritin levels. 48. Ritonavir increases deflazacort levels by affecting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 49. Ritonavir increases desipramine levels by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Ritonavir increases desvenlafaxine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to potential toxicity. 51. Ritonavir increases deutetrabenazine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Do not exceed 18 mg per dose or 36 mg per day of deutetrabenazine when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 52. Ritonavir increases dexamethasone levels by affecting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Ritonavir increases dexfenfluramine levels by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 54. Ritonavir increases dexlansoprazole levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Ritonavir increases dextroamphetamine levels by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 56. Ritonavir increases dextromethorphan levels by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 57. DHEA increases ritonavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Ritonavir increases diazepam levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 59. Ritonavir increases buccal diazepam levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
